DTW-Based Isolated Vowel Recognition¶

Submitted by - Faisal ziyad Ahmed (254102311)¶

Project 1: Perform DTW based isolated vowel recognition

• Record twenty five utterances of each of the isolated English digits (0-9), vowels (a,e,i,o,u),
and the given sentence (I'm registered with speech technology course and recording this data for the course project) in your voice. Record speech data over PC using Audacity software in PCM format with a sampling frequency of 16 kHz and a precision of 16-bits. Store the
recorded data as: <Roll.No>//sentence<recording_num>.wav. Human voice characteristics usually differ slightly over the time and it is referred to as the session
variation. So you are advised to record different entities at least in two sessions.

• For each of the vowels, choose one of the utterance as the reference template and the
remaining ones as the test templates. Compute 39-dimensional MFCC features comprising base, delta, and delta-delta components for all the recordings using MATLAB. Using DTW
command of MATLAB, write a script that computes DTW scores for any two similar or
dissimilar test utterances and also plots the corresponding DTW curve

Feature Extraction (39-dim MFCC)¶

In [26]:
def extract_features(file_path):
    """Load a wav file and return 39-dim MFCC matrix of shape (T, 39)."""
    y, sr = librosa.load(file_path, sr=SR)
    y, _  = librosa.effects.trim(y)   # remove leading/trailing silence

    mfcc   = librosa.feature.mfcc(y=y, sr=sr, n_mfcc=N_MFCC)
    delta  = librosa.feature.delta(mfcc)
    delta2 = librosa.feature.delta(mfcc, order=2)

    features = np.vstack((mfcc, delta, delta2))  # (39, T)
    return features.T                             # (T, 39)

DTW Computation¶

In [28]:
def compute_dtw(ref, test):
    """
    Compute DTW between two MFCC sequences.
    Returns:
        score      : normalized DTW distance (total cost / path length)
        D          : accumulated cost matrix
        path       : optimal warping path as list of (i, j) tuples
    """
    distance_matrix = cdist(ref, test, metric='euclidean')
    D = np.zeros_like(distance_matrix)

    D[0, 0] = distance_matrix[0, 0]

    for i in range(1, D.shape[0]):
        D[i, 0] = distance_matrix[i, 0] + D[i-1, 0]

    for j in range(1, D.shape[1]):
        D[0, j] = distance_matrix[0, j] + D[0, j-1]

    for i in range(1, D.shape[0]):
        for j in range(1, D.shape[1]):
            D[i, j] = distance_matrix[i, j] + min(
                D[i-1, j],
                D[i, j-1],
                D[i-1, j-1]
            )

    # ── Backtracking to recover optimal path ──
    i, j = D.shape[0] - 1, D.shape[1] - 1
    path = [(i, j)]

    while i > 0 and j > 0:
        steps = [D[i-1, j], D[i, j-1], D[i-1, j-1]]
        move  = np.argmin(steps)
        if move == 0:
            i -= 1
        elif move == 1:
            j -= 1
        else:
            i -= 1
            j -= 1
        path.append((i, j))

    path.reverse()

    # FIX: normalize by path length so scores are comparable across
    # pairs of different durations (raw score was in the thousands)
    normalized_score = D[-1, -1] / len(path)

    return normalized_score, D, path

Plot DTW Curve¶

This is the function the project asks you to plot: the cost matrix with the optimal warping path overlaid.

In [29]:
def plot_dtw(D, path, title="DTW Alignment"):
    """
    Plot the DTW accumulated cost matrix and the optimal warping path.
    D    : accumulated cost matrix  (shape: T_ref x T_test)
    path : list of (i, j) index tuples — the optimal warping path
    """
    path_i = [p[0] for p in path]
    path_j = [p[1] for p in path]

    plt.figure(figsize=(7, 5))
    plt.imshow(D, origin='lower', aspect='auto', cmap='viridis')
    plt.colorbar(label='Accumulated Cost')
    plt.plot(path_j, path_i, color='red', linewidth=2, label='Warping Path')
    plt.xlabel('Test Utterance Frames')
    plt.ylabel('Reference Utterance Frames')
    plt.title(title)
    plt.legend(loc='upper left')
    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.show()

Build Reference Templates¶

In [34]:
def build_references():
    """Use the first (sorted) file of each vowel folder as the reference template."""
    references = {}
    for vowel in VOWELS:                                       # VOWELS is now uppercase
        folder = os.path.join(DATASET_PATH, vowel)            # correctly finds A/ E/ etc.
        files  = sorted([f for f in os.listdir(folder) if f.endswith('.wav')])
        references[vowel] = extract_features(os.path.join(folder, files[0]))
        print(f"  Reference for '{vowel}': {files[0]}")
    return references

Recognition Function¶

In [35]:
def run_recognition():
    """
    For each vowel folder, skip the reference file (index 0) and
    classify the remaining 24 utterances by minimum DTW distance.
    """
    references = build_references()
    y_true = []
    y_pred = []

    for true_vowel in VOWELS:
        folder = os.path.join(DATASET_PATH, true_vowel)
        files  = sorted([f for f in os.listdir(folder) if f.endswith('.wav')])[1:]  # skip reference

        for file in files:
            test = extract_features(os.path.join(folder, file))

            # Score against all 5 reference templates
            scores = {}
            for ref_vowel in VOWELS:
                score, _, _ = compute_dtw(references[ref_vowel], test)
                scores[ref_vowel] = score

            prediction = min(scores, key=scores.get)   # nearest neighbour

            y_true.append(true_vowel)
            y_pred.append(prediction)

    return y_true, y_pred
